# The radius of the product of two polynomials whose coefficients are BallVectors

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `conv_radius` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Numbers of `T` that bound expressions of $m_a, m_b, r_x, r_y, m, g, t$ from above:

$$r_z \ge m ((1 + u) m_a r_y + (1 + u) m_b r_x + r_x r_y) + g m (1 + u)^{2} m_a m_b + t.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of the loop `bv_conv_1`, called by `convolution`, the product of polynomials, of `BallVector<T, 1, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 1>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_conv_2`, called by `convolution`, the product of polynomials, of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $m_a \ge 0$.
- $m_b \ge 0$.
- $r_x \ge 0$.
- $r_y \ge 0$.
- $m = 0$ or $m \ge 1$, as a number of terms is.
- $g \ge 0$.
- $g \le 1$.
- $t \ge 0$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $r_z \ge m ((1 + u) m_a r_y + (1 + u) m_b r_x + r_x r_y) + g m (1 + u)^{2} m_a m_b + t$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `conv_radius_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/BvConv.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/BvConv.v), against `conv_radius_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions conv_radius_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition conv_radius_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall ma mb rx ry m g t : R,
  fmt emin prec ma ->
  fmt emin prec mb ->
  fmt emin prec rx ->
  fmt emin prec ry ->
  fmt emin prec m ->
  fmt emin prec g ->
  fmt emin prec t ->
  0 <= ma ->
  0 <= mb ->
  0 <= rx ->
  0 <= ry ->
  (m = 0 \/ 1 <= m) ->
  0 <= g ->
  g <= 1 ->
  0 <= t ->
  let rz := conv_radius emin prec tie_even ma mb rx ry m g t in
  fmt emin prec rz /\
  (((m * (((((1 + u prec) * ma) * ry) + (((1 + u prec) * mb) * rx)) + (rx * ry))) + ((((g * m) * ((1 + u prec) ^ 2)) * ma) * mb)) + t) <= rz.
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `conv_radius_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/conv_radius.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/conv_radius.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The radius of a product of polynomials whose coefficients are BallVectors (milestone2.md, "The
# product of polynomials": conv_radius, the listing of the page). ma and mb are the largest |leading
# limb| of the centers of the two operands, rx and ry their radii, m the largest number of terms of a
# coefficient (the smaller of the two lengths, as a number of T rounded up), and g, t the exported
# bound of a dot product of m terms (bound_dot_k), g at most 1. Then
#   rz >= m ((1+u) ma ry + (1+u) mb rx + rx ry) + g m (1+u)^2 ma mb + t,
# the first part being what the radii of the operands become and the second the rounding of the
# centers, with the sum of |cx_i cy_j| of a coefficient bounded by m (1+u)^2 ma mb (a center is at most
# (1+u) times its leading limb). Every operation is a rounding to nearest of a nonnegative value: the
# product by (1+u)^7 covers the seven factors (1+u) that they lose, and hm the eta/2 that each of the
# five roundings before s can lose, multiplied by m, and the smallest normal number N, which keeps the
# radius normal (a chain of radius_4 of proofs/theories/Ball2.v, one link longer). Proposed in
# experiments/milestone2/kernels/ and checked there by batch.py and bv_conv.py, with this listing.

p  = prod(rx, ry)
q  = fma(mb, rx, p)
w  = fma(ma, ry, q)
ab = prod(ma, mb)
e  = fma(ab, g, w)
s  = fma(m, e, t)
hm = prod(m, const up(4*(1+u)^8*eta+eta/(2*u)))
rz = fma(s, const up((1+u)^7), hm)
```
